comments.body: Do you keep the raw input as well, or only the normalised number?
Both. Raw for support, normalised in a separate column with a unique index for lookups.
On the form, accept spaces and dashes silently and show the formatted version back. An error for a harmless space makes people think the form is broken.
Keep the raw. I once overwrote it with the clean version and could never tell later whether a number had been typed with the leading zero.
The library's metadata goes stale as operators add prefixes. Upgrade it now and then, and pin it so the upgrade is something you chose.
A valid format is not proof the person owns the number. Send a code before anything sensitive is linked to it.

title: Retire the nightly VACUUM FULL on bookings and tune autovacuum instead
body:
Every night at 02:00 a cron job runs VACUUM FULL on the bookings table (18 million rows, roughly 40 percent of them updated or deleted over a month). It takes an exclusive lock for about 6 minutes and the booking page stalls during it. Proposal: remove the job, set autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor to 0.02 and a higher cost limit for that one table, and watch dead tuples with a small Python script that reads pg_stat_user_tables every 10 minutes and warns above a threshold. Run pg_repack monthly if bloat still grows.

Cost: more background I/O during the day, and one more script to keep alive. Undecided: the warning threshold, and whether pg_repack is allowed on our hosting.

comments.body: pg_repack needs room for a full copy of the table plus indexes while it runs. Check the free disk before you plan around it.
And on managed Postgres the extension is often unavailable, or only reachable through the provider's own tool. Ask before assuming.
Do customers hit the lock window? We saw spinners on a booking page at night for shift workers and nobody linked it to the maintenance job for weeks.

body: Les pharmacies veulent l'interface en arabe, et j'ai découvert que mes composants Vue étaient pleins de margin-left et padding-right. Une journée de recherche et remplacement vers les propriétés logiques, margin-inline-start et compagnie, et la version RTL tient. Dans l'appli React Native, I18nManager.forceRTL ne s'applique qu'après un redémarrage de l'appli, ce qui m'a surpris la première fois.

comments.body: Les icônes de flèche aussi, il faut les retourner. Et pas toutes : une loupe ne se retourne pas.
Oui, j'ai une classe qui retourne seulement les flèches et les chevrons. Les autres icônes restent telles quelles.
Tailwind a des variantes pour ça, ms et me à la place de ml et mr. Si tu n'utilises pas Tailwind tu peux écrire ta feuille de style avec les propriétés logiques seulement.
Pense aux textes mélangés : dans une phrase en arabe, un numéro d'ordonnance en chiffres latins peut s'afficher à l'envers. L'élément bdi ou dir auto règle ça.

body: Une requête partait deux fois au chargement de la page de programmation. J'avais un watch avec immediate à true et, en plus, un appel dans onMounted. Les deux se déclenchaient au montage. J'ai gardé seulement le watch et le double appel a disparu. Rien de spectaculaire, mais je ne l'ai vu que dans l'onglet réseau, pas dans le code.

Rolled a model back by moving the champion alias to the previous version instead of redeploying the service. It took 20 seconds, against a 12 minute pipeline run. I should have wired it up a year ago, every earlier rollback was a small panic. The alias lives in the model registry and the service reloads it every minute.

comments.body: Do you keep the previous model's feature code too? Rolling back weights alone breaks if the preprocessing changed between versions.

body: Cancelling a ride from the app sometimes showed "driver arrived" for a second afterwards, because a late websocket message overwrote local state. Now each status carries a version number and the client ignores anything older than what it already shows. Obvious in hindsight, but it only showed up now and then.

comments.body: Is the version number from the server or from the client's clock?
Server side, a counter per ride. Client clocks drift and a phone with the wrong date would reject every real update.
